phase1_c1_vs_c2_gate.aggregation_correction: the -17.89pp pooled BABILong figure is a mean over 9 cells with OPPOSITE true signs (4 sig negative, 2 sig POSITIVE, 3 n.s.). Pooling summarises nothing. Report per-cell always. This is exactly the aggregation artifact A01's null-calibration protocol exists to catch.
phase1_c1_vs_c2_gate.no_clean_c2_advantage: There is NO protocol-clean benchmark on which C2 is significantly better in aggregate. The quarantined GPT-4o leg has been replaced by the open-weight Qwen3-8B result (+1.76pp, CI [-0.35,+3.78], CROSSES ZERO), which is also non-significant. Confirmed 2026-08-09.
phase1_c1_vs_c2_gate.prescribed_reframe: Position CoMem as a storage / read-compute method for high-reuse workloads, NOT a quality win. This is what the kill clause literally instructs.
phase1_c1_vs_c2_gate.reframe_NOT_supported: Do NOT reframe as 'C2 worse at exact-match, better at semantic'. qa5 lives INSIDE BABILong, a synthetic exact-match benchmark, so that split does not carve the data. The honest axis is single-span retrieval (C2 loses badly at long context) vs multi-mention relation (C2 can win), and that needs more than 2 significant cells to assert.
blocks: Do NOT build Configs 3/4/5 (~400 lines per status/proposal_prep/A02_CONFIG345_WIRING.md) on the premise that C2 is the strong quality arm -- the gate says it is not. If built, it should test the storage/read-compute framing, which needs a latency/storage axis.

f1_leg_retraction.retracted: the re-run's F1 leg (+0.68pp CI[+0.31,+1.02], reported as 'significantly positive / new minor finding')
f1_leg_retraction.reason: scripts/a02_judge_openweight.py:423-445 REIMPLEMENTED F1 instead of importing the canonical compute_f1/normalize_answer from eval_qcmem_locomo.py:313-343. Two bugs: (1) normalize_answer operation order swapped -- canonical does remove_punc THEN remove_articles, the re-run does remove_articles THEN remove_punc, so \b(a|an|the)\b lands on different word boundaries while punctuation is still present ('the-house' -> canonical 'thehouse' vs re-run 'house'; 'a.k.a. Bob' -> 'aka bob' vs 'k bob'; 'an-apple' -> 'anapple' vs 'apple'). (2) zero-overlap: canonical returns 0.0, the re-run `continue`s.
f1_leg_retraction.canonical_value: +0.20pp CI[-0.36,+0.75] -- a TIE. This is the value to cite, because it is the F1 definition every other LoCoMo number in this project used.
f1_leg_retraction.principle: using a different normaliser for one cell of a comparison table makes cross-row comparison meaningless regardless of which normaliser is better in the abstract
